prompt: My blood test shows low Hemoglobin (g/dL). In plain language, what does a low Hemoglobin result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Hemoglobin measures the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. This is called anemia. Common causes include iron deficiency, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, blood loss and long-term illness. It can cause tiredness, breathlessness and pale skin. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Hemoglobin (g/dL). In plain language, what does a high Hemoglobin result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Hemoglobin measures the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. This can happen with dehydration, smoking, living at high altitude, lung disease, or rarely a bone-marrow condition that makes too many red cells. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low White blood cells (WBC) (×10³/µL). In plain language, what does a low White blood cells (WBC) result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: White blood cells (WBC) measures the cells that fight infection. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low white cells can follow viral infections, some medicines, nutritional deficiencies or bone-marrow problems, and can make infections more likely. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high White blood cells (WBC) (×10³/µL). In plain language, what does a high White blood cells (WBC) result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: White blood cells (WBC) measures the cells that fight infection. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High white cells usually point to infection or inflammation. Stress, steroids and smoking can also raise them; very high counts need prompt review. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Platelets (×10³/µL). In plain language, what does a low Platelets result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Platelets measures the cell fragments that help blood clot. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low platelets are common in dengue and other viral fevers, and can also come from some medicines, liver disease or bone-marrow problems. Very low levels raise bleeding risk. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Platelets (×10³/µL). In plain language, what does a high Platelets result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Platelets measures the cell fragments that help blood clot. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High platelets often follow infection, inflammation, iron deficiency or surgery, and rarely a bone-marrow condition. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low MCV (red cell size) (fL). In plain language, what does a low MCV (red cell size) result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: MCV (red cell size) measures the average size of your red blood cells. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Small red cells are most often due to iron deficiency. Thalassemia trait is another common cause in India. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high MCV (red cell size) (fL). In plain language, what does a high MCV (red cell size) result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: MCV (red cell size) measures the average size of your red blood cells. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. Large red cells can come from vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol use, thyroid problems or some medicines. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Fasting glucose (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a low Fasting glucose result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Fasting glucose measures the sugar level in your blood after not eating overnight. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low fasting sugar can come from skipping meals, diabetes medicines or insulin, alcohol, or rarely hormone problems. It can cause shakiness, sweating and confusion. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Fasting glucose (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a high Fasting glucose result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Fasting glucose measures the sugar level in your blood after not eating overnight. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. 100 to 125 mg/dL is the prediabetes range; 126 mg/dL or more on repeat testing is in the diabetes range. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low HbA1c (%). In plain language, what does a low HbA1c result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: HbA1c measures your average blood sugar over the past two to three months. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. A low HbA1c is uncommon and can be affected by anemia, recent blood loss or some hemoglobin variants. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high HbA1c (%). In plain language, what does a high HbA1c result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: HbA1c measures your average blood sugar over the past two to three months. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. 5.7 to 6.4% is the prediabetes range and 6.5% or above is in the diabetes range. Anemia and some hemoglobin variants can affect this test. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Creatinine (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a low Creatinine result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Creatinine measures a waste product your kidneys filter out. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low creatinine usually reflects low muscle mass and is rarely a concern on its own. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Creatinine (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a high Creatinine result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Creatinine measures a waste product your kidneys filter out. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High creatinine can mean the kidneys are filtering less well. Dehydration, some painkillers and other medicines, and high-protein diets can also raise it. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Blood urea (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a low Blood urea result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Blood urea measures a protein waste product cleared by the kidneys. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low urea can come from a low-protein diet, liver disease or overhydration. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Blood urea (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a high Blood urea result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Blood urea measures a protein waste product cleared by the kidneys. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High urea can come from dehydration, reduced kidney function, a high-protein diet or bleeding in the gut. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low BUN (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a low BUN result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: BUN measures the nitrogen part of urea, cleared by the kidneys. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low BUN can come from a low-protein diet, liver disease or overhydration. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high BUN (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a high BUN result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: BUN measures the nitrogen part of urea, cleared by the kidneys. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High BUN can come from dehydration, reduced kidney function, a high-protein diet or bleeding in the gut. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Sodium (mmol/L). In plain language, what does a low Sodium result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Sodium measures a salt that controls fluid balance and nerve function. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low sodium can come from vomiting or diarrhoea, some blood-pressure medicines and diuretics, drinking a lot of water, or heart, liver and kidney conditions. Severe drops can cause confusion and seizures. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Sodium (mmol/L). In plain language, what does a high Sodium result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Sodium measures a salt that controls fluid balance and nerve function. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High sodium usually means the body is short of water, for example from dehydration or not drinking enough. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Potassium (mmol/L). In plain language, what does a low Potassium result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Potassium measures a salt that keeps your heart rhythm and muscles working. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low potassium can come from vomiting, diarrhoea or diuretics, and can cause weakness, cramps and heart-rhythm changes. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Potassium (mmol/L). In plain language, what does a high Potassium result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Potassium measures a salt that keeps your heart rhythm and muscles working. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High potassium can come from reduced kidney function or some blood-pressure medicines, and can affect heart rhythm. Very high levels are an emergency. A delayed or difficult blood draw can also falsely raise it. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high ALT (SGPT) (U/L). In plain language, what does a high ALT (SGPT) result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: ALT (SGPT) measures an enzyme released when liver cells are irritated or damaged. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. Raised ALT is most often due to fatty liver, alcohol, viral hepatitis or medicines. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high AST (SGOT) (U/L). In plain language, what does a high AST (SGOT) result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: AST (SGOT) measures an enzyme found in the liver, heart and muscles. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. Raised AST can come from liver conditions, alcohol, heavy exercise or muscle injury. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Total bilirubin (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a high Total bilirubin result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Total bilirubin measures a yellow pigment made when old red cells break down and cleared by the liver. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High bilirubin can cause jaundice. Causes include liver inflammation, blocked bile ducts, faster breakdown of red cells, or Gilbert's syndrome, a harmless inherited condition. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Total cholesterol (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a high Total cholesterol result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Total cholesterol measures the total amount of cholesterol carried in your blood. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High cholesterol raises long-term heart and stroke risk, especially together with high LDL and low HDL. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high LDL cholesterol (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a high LDL cholesterol result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: LDL cholesterol measures the 'bad' cholesterol that can build up in artery walls. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High LDL is a major risk factor for heart attack and stroke. Diet, activity, family history and medicines all affect it. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low HDL cholesterol (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a low HDL cholesterol result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: HDL cholesterol measures the 'good' cholesterol that helps clear fat from arteries. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low HDL raises heart risk. Inactivity, smoking, excess weight and high triglycerides often go with it. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Triglycerides (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a high Triglycerides result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Triglycerides measures a type of fat in the blood that rises with sugar, refined carbs and alcohol. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High triglycerides add to heart risk and often go with diabetes, excess weight and alcohol use. Very high levels can inflame the pancreas. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low TSH (mIU/L). In plain language, what does a low TSH result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: TSH measures the brain's signal telling the thyroid how hard to work. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low TSH usually means the thyroid is overactive or thyroid medicine is too high. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high TSH (mIU/L). In plain language, what does a high TSH result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: TSH measures the brain's signal telling the thyroid how hard to work. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High TSH usually means the thyroid is underactive. Tiredness, weight gain and feeling cold are common symptoms. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Free T4 (ng/dL). In plain language, what does a low Free T4 result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Free T4 measures the main hormone made by the thyroid. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low free T4 suggests an underactive thyroid. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Free T4 (ng/dL). In plain language, what does a high Free T4 result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Free T4 measures the main hormone made by the thyroid. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High free T4 suggests an overactive thyroid or too much thyroid medicine. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Ferritin (ng/mL). In plain language, what does a low Ferritin result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Ferritin measures your body's iron stores. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low ferritin means iron stores are low. This is the most common cause of anemia, often from diet, heavy periods or blood loss. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Ferritin (ng/mL). In plain language, what does a high Ferritin result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Ferritin measures your body's iron stores. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High ferritin can come from inflammation, infection, liver disease or iron overload. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Vitamin B12 (pg/mL). In plain language, what does a low Vitamin B12 result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Vitamin B12 measures a vitamin needed for nerves and red blood cells. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low B12 is common in vegetarian diets and with some medicines like metformin. It can cause tiredness, tingling and anemia. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Vitamin B12 (pg/mL). In plain language, what does a high Vitamin B12 result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Vitamin B12 measures a vitamin needed for nerves and red blood cells. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High B12 is usually from supplements or injections and is rarely a problem on its own. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Vitamin D (25-OH) (ng/mL). In plain language, what does a low Vitamin D (25-OH) result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Vitamin D (25-OH) measures a vitamin for bones, muscles and immunity. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low vitamin D is very common, especially with little sun exposure. It can cause bone pain and muscle weakness. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Vitamin D (25-OH) (ng/mL). In plain language, what does a high Vitamin D (25-OH) result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Vitamin D (25-OH) measures a vitamin for bones, muscles and immunity. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High vitamin D almost always comes from taking too many supplements. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high CRP (mg/L). In plain language, what does a high CRP result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: CRP measures a general marker of inflammation in the body. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High CRP signals inflammation, most often from infection, and also from injury or autoimmune conditions. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows low Uric acid (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a low Uric acid result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Uric acid measures a waste product from breaking down purines in food. A low result means your value is below the usual reference range. Low uric acid is uncommon and rarely a concern. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My blood test shows high Uric acid (mg/dL). In plain language, what does a high Uric acid result mean, what are common causes, and when should I see a doctor?
completion: Uric acid measures a waste product from breaking down purines in food. A high result means your value is above the usual reference range. High uric acid can lead to gout and kidney stones. Alcohol, red meat, sugary drinks and kidney problems can raise it. One result alone is not a diagnosis; your doctor will read it alongside your symptoms and other tests.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: low counts across red cells, white cells and platelets. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: All three blood cell types are low together. This can happen with severe infections, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, some medicines, or problems in the bone marrow where blood cells are made. It needs prompt review by a doctor. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: reduced kidney clearance with high potassium. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: High creatinine suggests the kidneys are filtering less well, and high potassium can build up when they do. High potassium can affect heart rhythm, so this combination should be checked by a doctor the same day. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: liver enzymes raised together with bilirubin. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: Raised liver enzymes with raised bilirubin suggest the liver is inflamed or bile flow is blocked. Causes include viral hepatitis, alcohol, medicines and gallstones. This should be reviewed by a doctor soon. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: liver enzymes raised together. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: ALT and AST both rising points to irritation of liver cells. In India the most common causes are fatty liver, alcohol, viral hepatitis and some medicines. A doctor may suggest an ultrasound or repeat tests. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: kidney filtration markers raised together. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: Creatinine and urea both clear through the kidneys, so when both are high it points to reduced kidney filtration. Dehydration can do this too. A doctor may repeat the test and check your eGFR and urine. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: anemia alongside reduced kidney function. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: The kidneys make a hormone that tells the body to produce red blood cells. When kidney function drops, anemia often follows. A doctor can check whether these two results are linked. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: pattern of iron-deficiency anemia. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: Low hemoglobin with small red blood cells is the typical pattern of iron-deficiency anemia, the most common anemia in India. Thalassemia trait can look similar. A doctor will look for the cause, such as diet or blood loss. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: pattern of b12 or folate-deficiency anemia. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: Low hemoglobin with large red blood cells is typical of vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. This is common with vegetarian diets and with some medicines like metformin. Treatment is usually simple once the cause is confirmed. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: blood sugar results in the diabetes range. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: When fasting glucose and HbA1c are both in the diabetes range, it strongly suggests diabetes. A doctor will confirm the diagnosis and discuss diet, activity and medicines. Early control lowers the risk of complications. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: blood sugar above normal. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: Your sugar results are above the normal range but do not meet the full diabetes criteria on both tests. This is often called prediabetes, and lifestyle changes can bring it back to normal. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: metabolic syndrome pattern. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: High triglycerides, low HDL and raised blood sugar often appear together as metabolic syndrome. This combination raises the risk of heart disease and diabetes more than any single result. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: cholesterol pattern linked to heart risk. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: High LDL together with low HDL or high triglycerides increases the build-up of fat in arteries. A doctor may estimate your overall heart risk and suggest diet, exercise or medicines. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: underactive thyroid pattern. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: High TSH with low free T4 is the typical pattern of an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism). It is common and treatable with a daily tablet. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: mildly underactive thyroid pattern. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: TSH is high but free T4 is still normal. This is often called subclinical hypothyroidism. Doctors usually repeat the test in a few weeks before deciding on treatment. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: overactive thyroid pattern. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: Low TSH with high free T4 is the typical pattern of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism). It can cause a fast heartbeat, weight loss and anxiety, and should be reviewed by a doctor. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: signs of active infection or inflammation. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: High white cells together with high CRP usually mean the body is fighting an infection or significant inflammation. A doctor will match this with your symptoms, such as fever. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: pattern suggesting dehydration. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: High urea and sodium with normal creatinine is often seen when the body is short of water. Drinking enough fluids and repeating the test usually clarifies it. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.

prompt: My lab report shows this combination: high uric acid with reduced kidney clearance. What can it mean together, and what should I do next?
completion: The kidneys clear uric acid, so it can rise when kidney function drops. Together these raise the risk of gout and kidney stones. This is not a diagnosis; please discuss it with your doctor.
